concept.name: Morning star
concept.definition: A three-candlestick bottom reversal pattern: a long black body is followed by a small-bodied candle (the star, of either color) that gaps below the first body, and then a long white body that closes well into the first candle's real body. Technical analysts treat it as a major bottom reversal signal marking a shift from selling to indecision to buying.
concept.intuition: Sellers push hard, then the market stalls in a small indecisive candle, then buyers take over and recover most of the lost ground, like dawn after a dark night.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long black body in a downtrend; candle 2 has a small real body (ideally gapping below body 1); candle 3 is a long white body closing above the midpoint of body 1. The gap between bodies 1 and 2 (and ideally between 2 and 3) is the classic requirement, often relaxed in gap-poor markets.
concept.failure_modes: In gapless markets (spot forex, crypto) the pattern is frequently identified without true gaps, which weakens it. A weak third candle that fails to close deep into the first body often precedes renewed decline.
concept.misconceptions: The star need not be a doji; any small body qualifies (when it is a doji the pattern is specifically a morning doji star). The pattern is also not complete, and not actionable by convention, until the third candle closes.
concept.example: A stock slides, printing a long black candle (52.00 to 50.00), then a tiny-bodied candle around 49.60-49.80, then a long white candle closing at 51.50, deep into the first body. Chartists read the morning star as a bottom reversal signal.
